threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus to arrive on time – locals know it’s always late, so they just grab a coffee and chill.
Last night on the 78, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old 90s R&B. Most got into it, but the driver looked ready to call it a night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy setting up a DJ booth in his living room, blasting techno while his cat lounged on the windowsill. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find open-air clubs where people dance in the street until sunrise, often with a spontaneous BBQ on the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name at least three taco trucks on the same block without missing a beat. Out-of-towners just look at their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that had a guy playing the ukulele. He went from 'Somewhere Over the Rainbow' to a spirited rendition of 'California Love'—only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think paella is a daily thing. Locals actually save it for special occasions—it's more of a festive feast than a regular meal.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still stare at the Sagrada Família like it's a unicorn—locals just walk past it, barely glancing.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 48 bus is the best way to get anywhere, but everyone knows it's all about those hidden shortcuts through the backstreets.
Caught a guy on the 35 last night passionately debating the merits of Jerk versus KFC without a pause. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized this place was home when I saw the late-night kebab shop owner sharing a laugh with the police. It’s just another Tuesday in the Kiez.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find spontaneous outdoor cinema screenings in the middle of a parking lot. Just grab a beer and settle in.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows not to bother asking for 'regular' on a Friday at La Taqueria. You’ll just be waiting twice as long.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy trying to coax a pigeon onto the 19 bus today. The driver's just shaking his head like this is a normal Tuesday in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all hipster bars; they miss the hidden bakeries where locals line up for fresh pa de xapó every morning.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival in Gràcia by their bewilderment when they try to navigate the narrow streets—totally missing the hidden plazas and the best tapas spots.
